knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Semantic type loss during object deserialization
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Serialization and deserialization APIs may reconstruct objects with generic tensor types instead of preserving framework-specific wrapper types and associated execution state.

risk_dimensions.shape: Parameter tensor shapes ranging from scalar to nested and zero-size dimensions
risk_dimensions.dtype: Non-default tensor dtypes and requires_grad-related dtype/state combinations
risk_dimensions.memory: Shared or nested object graphs that must retain identity and storage relationships
risk_dimensions.device: Serialized objects originally placed on different devices
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Framework-specific wrappers such as parameter types and gradient tracking metadata

failure_mechanism.description: Deserialization can reconstruct stored objects using generic tensor types and fail to restore framework-specific wrapper metadata, causing silent semantic downgrades.

input_exploration: Vary nesting depth and placement of stateful wrapper objects
Explore different tensor shapes, dtypes, requires_grad values, and device placements
Include shared references and nested module-like structures
Test both top-level and deeply nested parameter-bearing objects
constraint_awareness: Serialization should preserve semantic wrapper types rather than only tensor values
Execution state such as requires_grad may be attached to wrapper objects
Deserialization may silently succeed while losing type identity
oracle_strategy: Assert that restored objects retain their original framework-specific wrapper types
Compare execution state metadata such as requires_grad before and after deserialization
Detect silent type downgrades that do not raise exceptions

transferability.reason: Any persistence or checkpointing API that serializes rich object graphs with semantic wrapper types may lose type identity and execution state, so the testing principle applies broadly beyond the original API.

important_considerations: Focus on preservation of semantic wrapper types across serialization boundaries
Consider nested object graphs and shared references
Detect silent loss of execution state that does not trigger errors
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that construct objects with framework-specific semantic wrappers, serialize them through the target persistence API, deserialize them, and verify type and execution-state invariants rather than only numerical equality.
